turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to start with how my son found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class. Who decided that, and before or after anyone spoke to me?
Fine. Finish. But I asked who decided and when, and I'm writing down that I don't have an answer yet.
I have 140 students. I don't have time to be cross-examined by every parent with a law degree.
That's not Owen's problem, Hale. You asked for this meeting, so it's one parent and one question: was my son heard before that zero went in, or after?
You don't get to talk to me like I'm on the stand.

Then answer it like a teacher. Your school's own procedure, 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Either you explain that, or I'm in the principal's office when we're done.
